title: Payment connection pool timeouts
executive_summary: INC-012: payment-service connection pool timeouts began at ~10:06Z, after config-bot reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 10 at 10:04Z (ticket OPS-2669). Pool saturation (active=10, idle=0, waiting up to 92) followed within about one minute, and error rate rose from ~0.8% to ~17% and timeouts from ~0.1% to ~11-13%. The pool-size cut is the most likely cause. A connection leak (prior-year pattern) is not supported because the saturation step coincides with the config change, not a gradual build-up.

hypotheses.description: Config change db.pool.max_size 50->10 on payment-service at 10:04Z caused the DB connection pool to saturate under normal load (~300 rps), producing acquisition timeouts and errors. Mechanism: Pool capped at 10 connections; with steady load, all connections are active (active=10, idle=0) and waiting requests queue until the 5000ms acquisition timeout, which then fails the request. DB connection utilisation goes 35% -> 100% (onset 10:05) and errors/timeouts step up at 10:06.

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): configuration_regression in payment-service - Config change db.pool.max_size 50->10 on payment-service at 10:04Z caused the DB connection pool to saturate under normal load (~300 rps), producing acquisition timeouts and errors.
corrective_actions: Revert db.pool.max_size on payment-service from 10 to the prior value of 50 (or the validated value per OPS-2669) and verify conn util, error rate and timeouts return to baseline
Restart or roll pods only if connections remain stuck after the revert
preventive_actions: Add config validation in CI/CD or config-bot that blocks large pool-size reductions (for example >50%) without approval
Require review for db pool changes on payment-service
Add a pre-change load test for pool sizing
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on db_conn_util_pct > 80% sustained for 2 minutes on payment-service
Alert on pool acquisition timeout log rate and error_rate > 2%
Track config changes to db.pool.* keys as annotated events on dashboards

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The incident is most likely caused by the config change db.pool.max_size 50 -> 10 at 10:04Z on payment-service (cfg-56d39584). The change precedes the utilisation rise (10:05), the error and timeout rise (10:06), and the pool-timeout logs, which show active=10 idle=0 consistent with the new cap. Request rate and CPU were flat, which rules out traffic surge and compute saturation. The connection-leak analogy from last year is not supported by the step-change timing. Revert the setting to restore service. Remaining gaps: intent of OPS-2669, whether the value is live on all pods, and DB-side data.
